misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: A local signer is a component of the node itself, not an external entity. The private key is stored locally and the signing process is internal to the node's operation. The actual external entity is the transaction submitters whose transactions the signer includes in blocks.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External entity that produces blocks which must meet the calculated difficulty target
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Miners are economically incentivized through block rewards but their blocks are not inherently trusted. Every block must pass difficulty validation and PoW verification before acceptance. Trust extends only to computational proof, not to block content validity.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: Proof-of-work - blocks must demonstrate sufficient computational work

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Network peer that sends blocks for validation
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Peers are unauthenticated network participants. Any node can propagate blocks regardless of validity. The entire difficulty validation mechanism exists because peer-relayed blocks cannot be trusted without verification.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - blocks validated locally regardless of source

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Other nodes in the Clique network propagating blocks
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Network peers in Clique are not authenticated at the network layer. Blocks received from peers must be validated by extracting the signer, verifying authorization, checking signing limits, and validating timestamps. The peer itself is never trusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - block signer verified via ECDSA signature in extraData

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Current member of the authorized signer set proposing votes
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Authorized signers are identified by their cryptographic keys and added via governance voting. They are trusted to sign blocks and propose votes, but multiple security controls limit abuse: signing limits prevent spam, majority voting required for changes, and any signer can be voted out. Trust is conditional on continued honest majority behavior.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: ECDSA signature - signers identified by recovered address from block signature

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External account deploying a new smart contract
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any account can submit contract deployment transactions. The deployer's code is arbitrary and potentially malicious. The 0xEF byte check exists precisely because deployers cannot be trusted to provide valid bytecode - the system must enforce the EOF format reservation.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: ECDSA signature - proves account ownership but not code safety

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Trusted party providing the weak subjectivity checkpoint for initial synchronization
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Node operators are explicitly trusted to provide valid weak subjectivity checkpoints. This is an intentional trust assumption in the EIP - the specification acknowledges this creates a trust dependency. However, checkpoints can be validated against known state roots once received.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: Out-of-band trust - operator provides checkpoint via manual configuration

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Other execution client in the P2P network providing block data
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Network peers providing block data are unauthenticated. Block data must be validated against expected state roots and chain rules before being stored. The pruning mechanism doesn't change the trust level - peers have always been untrusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - data validated via consensus rules

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Peer node requesting historical block data via devp2p protocol
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Peers requesting data are unauthenticated. They can request any data but the node serving data doesn't need to trust the requester - it simply evaluates whether to serve based on local policy (age of data). The requester has no special privileges.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Application requiring historical blockchain data for business logic
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: dApps requesting historical data are simply consumers. They have no special trust - they receive data that must be validated. The dApp can request any data but the response may be unavailable if data has been pruned.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - RPC requests are unauthenticated queries

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Out-of-band historical data source (IPFS, Portal Network, The Graph, torrent)
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: External data providers supply historical data that MUST be validated. The EIP explicitly notes this as a security consideration - data from external sources requires integrity verification against known state roots. No inherent trust in the provider.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - data must be cryptographically verified against accumulators/state roots

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Web application requesting chain switch via wallet RPC
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: dApps can request chain switches but these are untrusted requests. The entire EIP specifies security controls (URL sanitization, SSRF detection, phishing checks, user confirmation) precisely because dApp chain switch requests cannot be trusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - requests are arbitrary web3 calls

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Human user interacting with wallet UI to approve/reject requests
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Users are the ultimate authority for wallet actions - they approve or reject chain switches. However, users may be deceived by phishing attempts. The security model relies on users making informed decisions, hence the warnings and validation before presenting choices.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: Local wallet interaction - user has physical access to device

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External Ethereum RPC server provided by dApp
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: RPC endpoints are provided by potentially malicious dApps. They must be sanitized for SSRF attacks, verified to respond correctly (net_version, eth_chainId), and checked against known chain configurations. No trust in the endpoint itself.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - responses validated by comparison with expected values

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Attacker-controlled application attempting SSRF or phishing
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Explicitly modeled as an attacker. This entity represents the threat model - attackers attempting to exploit the chain switching mechanism via SSRF (targeting internal resources) or phishing (fake chain parameters). All inputs from this entity are hostile.

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Block propagated via P2P from peer nodes in Clique network
Authorized signer includes vote proposal in produced block header
Contract deployer submits transaction with init code that produces runtime bytecode
Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint as bootstrap for sync
Peer transmits block data via devp2p for storage
Peer requests historical block data via devp2p
External data source provides historical blocks for validation
dApp calls wallet_updateEthereumChain to request chain switch
Attacker sends crafted chain switch request with SSRF or phishing payload

coverage_gaps.reason: Implicit boundary - miners submit blocks which enter via peer propagation. Edge covered by EXT-PEER-NODE.
Block validation subgraph; external entity modeled but specific boundary edge not shown in validation flow - blocks arrive implicitly.
User interacts with UI, not direct data input to system. User provides approval decision via local wallet interface.
RPC endpoint receives requests FROM the wallet, doesn't send data INTO the system. Responses are fetched by wallet validation.
dApp queries for historical data, doesn't send data into system. Query responses flow outbound.

coverage_analysis.notes: EIP-4345 Arrow Glacier is a simple difficulty bomb delay with minimal external entity interaction. EIP-225 Clique has well-defined trust boundaries for peer blocks and authorized signer votes. EIP-3541 has a single external entity (deployer) with clear boundary. EIP-4444 introduces multiple external data sources requiring careful trust analysis. EIP-2015 explicitly models attacker threats (SSRF, phishing) as external entities.
